VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The following boundary conditions were examined and found harmless. (1) The existence of an inductive set is guaranteed by the Axiom of Infinity; without it the claim would be vacuous. (2) The Separation instance uses the formula φ(x) = ∀J (Inductive(J) → x ∈ J). This formula is first-order after expanding the defined predicate Inductive, and the universal quantifier over all sets is permitted in ZFC. (3) The definition of ω is impredicative (ω belongs to the collection of all inductive sets over which it quantifies), but full Separation in ZFC admits impredicative definitions. (4) The intersection is not empty because every inductive set contains ∅ by definition. (5) The successor operation x ↦ x∪{x} is legitimate via Pairing and Union, which are part of ZFC. (6) The uniqueness argument requires only that ω and ω′ satisfy the two stated properties, and the proof correctly derives equality from Extensionality. No counterexample to the claim or to the logical validity of the proof steps was found.
